About the data and credits

Tap any river on the map to see its year. The ring marks the spot shown in the graph.

Daily river flow comes from the GloFAS v5.0 hydrological reanalysis. It is a computer model of rain, snow, soil and rivers driven by weather records, so it is close to, but not the same as, gauge measurements.

Each stretch of river takes its flow from the 5 km model cell that drains the same catchment, so flood pulses travel downstream as they did in 2025. Rivers draining at least 150 km² are shown.

About 700 rivers and lochs are named. In Great Britain the names come from Ordnance Survey's OS Open Rivers, matched to each stretch by position. In Northern Ireland they come from DAERA's river water bodies. In Ireland each river was placed using a town it flows through and followed along the network. Some small streams are left unnamed.

River width shows how much water is flowing (it grows with the square root of discharge). In "Wet or dry", colour compares each stretch with its own median flow for 2025. Each day is the average flow over the 24 hours ending that day.

Discharge: GloFAS v5.0 reanalysis, Copernicus Emergency Management Service. Rivers: HydroRIVERS v1.0 (HydroSHEDS). Coastline: Natural Earth. River names in Great Britain contain OS data © Crown copyright and database right 2026. Northern Ireland river names: DAERA, Open Government Licence v3.0.
